extracted.intended_audience: general readers interested in media/journalism controversies; journalists, media critics, and those following BBC/trans issues
extracted.subtask_description: An encyclopedic summary and analysis of a single BBC News article and the subsequent public, internal, and regulatory criticisms about its editorial choices, sourcing, and harms. Focuses on how the article was produced, edited, received, and judged against BBC editorial standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy (BBC editorial rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles must be accurate; the Executive Complaints Unit found the piece breached the corporation's editorial rules on accuracy for not making clear the statistical invalidity of the Get the L Out poll and for a title that misleadingly suggested the article focused on pressure from trans women.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure factual claims are supported and that statistics or surveys are clearly qualified. Avoid headlines that give a misleading impression of the article's central focus. Example anti-patterns: presenting a small, self-selected poll as if it represented the wider community; using a headline that overstates or misattributes findings in the body.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of surveys — clarity about representativeness and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: The BBC was criticised for incorporating a social media poll that had a low sample size and self-selection bias and for not making sufficiently clear that it lacked statistical validity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using self-published or non-representative surveys, explicitly state their limitations (sample size, sampling method, geographic composition, self-selection). Avoid using such surveys 'in a way which leads our audience to believe they are more robust than they are.' Where possible, prefer representative data or independent studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartiality and range of views
rubrics_metrics.description: The BBC defended the article on the basis of its 'strong commitment to impartiality' and argued the report 'looks at a complex subject from different perspectives'. Critics said the article's interviewees had a narrow range of viewpoints and lacked countervailing voices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a genuine range of informed perspectives, especially on contested issues. Do not present disproportionately one-sided testimony without clear contextualisation. Anti-pattern: quoting primarily groups or figures known to push one agenda without including credible dissenting or representative voices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection and representation of sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Critics argued Lowbridge's chosen interviewees had a narrow range of viewpoints; others said the article 'does not contain a single interview with someone who disagrees that trans women are coercing lesbians into sex'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek diverse, representative sources relevant to the topic (including those directly affected and experts). Where high-profile individuals were contacted but declined, document attempts and be transparent. Avoid over-reliance on interlocutors from organisations with clear ideological aims without context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vetting and contextualising contributors' backgrounds and conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: The BBC later stated an 'admission of inappropriate behaviour' by a contributor should have been included; Lily Cade's quotes were removed after she published calls for violence and had prior sexual misconduct allegations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vet contributors for relevant past conduct that bears on credibility or public safety. Include materially relevant allegations or admissions about contributors when they affect the reliability or safety implications of quoted material. Anti-pattern: quoting contributors uncritically when they have publicly advocated violence or face serious allegations that alter context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding platforming violent or extremist rhetoric
rubrics_metrics.description: After publication, Lily Cade published blog posts calling for the 'lynching' of trans women; the BBC removed her contributions from the article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not publish or amplify explicit calls for violence or hate. If previously published material includes such rhetoric, correct, remove, or clearly contextualise it and consider the harm in retaining it. Editorial policy should prohibit uncritical platforming of violent extremism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline accuracy — reflect article focus
rubrics_metrics.description: The ECU found the original headline 'gave the misleading impression that the focus of the article would be on pressure applied by trans women' when the article actually focused equally on internalised pressure experienced by lesbians.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft headlines that accurately reflect the article's primary content and emphasis. Avoid sensational or misleading headlines that imply conclusions not supported by the text. Where nuance is central, ensure the headline does not distort balance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate assignment of reporters / subject expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Fran Unsworth said the article 'would have been better handled by an LGBTQ correspondent'; staff argued that handling by specialist reporters could have altered outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign sensitive or specialist topics to reporters with appropriate subject knowledge and experience. Editorial oversight should consider whether a regional commissioning process or a reporter without relevant beat expertise is the right choice. Anti-pattern: treating complex identity-related stories as general-interest regional pieces without specialist input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal editorial review and responsiveness to staff concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: There were internal debates and 'pushback' within BBC staff prior to publication; younger staff publicly criticised the article afterwards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain robust internal review processes that seriously consider editorial pushback and staff concerns. Document and act on substantive internal critiques, particularly when staff point to potential harms or inaccuracies. Ensure decisions are defensible and accountable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency about sourcing attempts and editorial judgments
rubrics_metrics.description: Lowbridge said several high-profile trans women were contacted but 'none of them wanted to speak'; BBC later justified describing someone as 'not high-profile' as a 'matter of judgement'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be transparent about who was contacted, who declined, and why certain sources or quotes were included or excluded. Where terms like 'high-profile' affect perception, explain editorial judgments to avoid misleading readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include materially relevant allegations about quoted individuals
rubrics_metrics.description: The BBC acknowledged that allegations against a quoted contributor (Lily Cade) should have been mentioned in the original article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a quoted individual's past conduct or allegations bear on their testimony's credibility or public safety, mention them in the reporting. Failure to do so can mislead readers and harm credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextualising activist-group material and rhetoric
rubrics_metrics.description: The article used material from the anti-trans campaign group Get the L Out and the LGB Alliance; critics noted these groups have discriminatory aims and the survey language invoked charged sources (e.g., Janice Raymond).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using material from advocacy groups, note their orientation, methodology, and potential biases. Do not present partisan or ideologically framed material as neutral fact. Provide context for quotations from polemical sources and clarify when their outputs are not representative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical validity — sample size and self-selection bias
rubrics_metrics.description: The Get the L Out survey had eighty responses and was distributed within the group's networks; critics flagged self-selection bias and small sample size as violating BBC guidelines when presented without qualification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report survey results with clear statements about sample size, sampling frame, geographic breakdown, and selection biases. Avoid implying representativeness when data are from small, self-selected samples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessing potential harm from international dissemination
rubrics_metrics.description: Concerns were raised about the article being internationalised to Brazil, where violence against trans people had surged, and whether that could exacerbate harms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the risks of translating or promoting sensitive content in jurisdictions where it may increase harm to vulnerable groups. Editorial decisions about international distribution should weigh local contexts and potential for real-world consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding use of community-rejected or loaded terminology without context
rubrics_metrics.description: The article used terms such as 'cotton ceiling' (rejected by the transgender community) and 'gold star lesbian' (criticised), which carry contested meanings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid uncritically using jargon or slurs that communities reject; when such terms are used, explain their contested nature and origins. Be cautious of language that implicitly delegitimises identities or reduces people to genital-based definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balancing 'platforming' and giving voice to harmed communities
rubrics_metrics.description: Some critics argued the piece 'contributes to irrational fearmongering aimed at trans women' while others said it gave space to lesbians who reported harm; the BBC argued the report looked at different perspectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strive for reporting that neither silences legitimate accounts of harm nor amplifies damaging stereotypes. Where testimonies of harm exist, corroborate, contextualise, and avoid generalising individual accounts into broader claims without evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-publication corrections and editorial accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: Following complaints, the BBC removed Cade's comments, altered wording around the survey, and changed the article title after an ECU ruling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have clear processes for correcting, updating, and explaining editorial changes after publication. Transparently record what was changed and why, and be prompt in addressing substantive breaches of standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding reliance on deleted or unavailable source material without clear provenance
rubrics_metrics.description: The article summarised previously expressed views of YouTubers and a poet, including one YouTuber who had already deleted the quoted video.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When citing material that has been deleted or is no longer publicly available, provide provenance and explain limitations on verification. Avoid heavy reliance on ephemeral online content without archiving or corroboration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corroboration and evidence for claims from organisational spokespeople
rubrics_metrics.description: Bev Jackson of LGB Alliance claimed a 'sizeable minority' pressuring lesbians but 'was unable to provide statistics.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask organisational spokespeople for evidence to substantiate claims; if none is available, make that absence clear to readers. Present anecdotal claims as such, not as data.
